Summarize diagnosis-position sensitivity

Source: R/dx-sensitivity.R
nis_dx_sensitivity.Rd

Summarizes unweighted and weighted presentation counts and outcome rates for principal, secondary-only, and any-position diagnosis flags. These are descriptive point estimates, not design-based survey estimates; use nis_design() when standard errors are needed. Small cells must go through nis_suppress() before reporting under the HCUP Data Use Agreement, which prohibits reporting cells of 1–10.

Usage

nis_dx_sensitivity(
  .data,
  code,
  system = c("icd10", "icd9"),
  weight_var = "DISCWT",
  outcomes = c("DIED", "ELECTIVE")
)

Arguments

.data

A data frame or lazy Arrow query.

code

Non-missing character vector of diagnosis prefixes.

system

Code system of the diagnosis slots: "icd10" (default) or "icd9" (experimental, NIS 2012 to Q3 2015).

weight_var

Name of the discharge weight column. Defaults to DISCWT.

outcomes

Outcome columns to summarize. By default, DIED and ELECTIVE are included when present and absent defaults are skipped.

Value

A collected tibble with one row per presentation and unweighted and weighted counts, shares of all prefix-positive presentations, and rates for requested outcomes. The principal presentation is a strict subset of any-position cases, so Cohen's kappa is not meaningful here.

See also

Code transitions and sensitivity.

Other cohort-definition: nis_attrition(), nis_audit_code_transition(), nis_ccsr_codes(), nis_flag_dx(), nis_flag_dx_position(), nis_flag_pr(), nis_flag_pr_timing(), nis_prday_completeness()

Examples

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019))
nis_dx_sensitivity(nis, "I50")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 9
#>   presentation n_unweighted n_weighted pct_of_any_unweighted pct_of_any_weighted
#>   <chr>               <dbl>      <dbl>                 <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1 principal              54       62.4                   100                 100
#> 2 secondary_o…            0        0                       0                   0
#> 3 any                    54       62.4                   100                 100
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: DIED_rate_unweighted <dbl>, DIED_rate_weighted <dbl>,
#> #   ELECTIVE_rate_unweighted <dbl>, ELECTIVE_rate_weighted <dbl>
